items.item_text: Knowledge and experience working with a diverse population, and sensitivity to culture, race, ethnicity, gender identity, sexual orientation, and socio-economic status.
Experience supporting educationally disadvantaged and academically at-risk populations and their families regarding postsecondary opportunities and careers. (Preferred)

Coordinate and manage meetings, convening, and regional events. Plan and support the successful execution of partner meetings, workgroups, academies, convenings, trainings, and other regional events, including scheduling, logistics, room reservations, catering, materials, registration, technology needs, and day-of event support.

Support partner communication and relationship management. Serve as a professional point of contact for K–12, postsecondary, workforce, community, and regional partners by coordinating communication, responding to inquiries, tracking follow-up items, and helping maintain strong, responsive working relationships across partnership initiatives.

Develop and distribute partner communications and newsletters. Assist with the development, organization, and distribution of regular partner updates, newsletters, announcements, event invitations, and other communications that highlight project activities, deadlines, partner successes, and opportunities for engagement.

Track project activities, deliverables, and follow-up actions. Maintain organized records of meeting notes, attendance, partner contacts, event participation, timelines, deliverables, and next steps to support project implementation, reporting, and accountability across multiple regional initiatives.

Prepare materials and support facilitation needs for partnership activities. Develop, format, and organize agendas, slide decks, handouts, sign-in sheets, surveys, briefing documents, and follow-up materials needed for partner meetings, workgroups, events, and technical assistance activities.

Provide administrative and operational support for regional alliance initiatives. Support the day-to-day coordination of K–20 Regional Alliances projects by assisting with calendar management, purchasing and fiscal processes, travel arrangements, vendor coordination, data collection support, and other administrative tasks that ensure smooth project operations.
Bachelor’s degree in early childhood or elementary school education or related area and three years of progressively responsible related experience or equivalent experience/training. (Required)
Master’s degree in related area from an accredited institution. (Preferred)
3 years of progressively responsible related experience and/or combination of experience and training. (Required)
Five years of progressively responsible related experience and /or combination of experience and training. (Preferred)
Able to travel and work evenings and weekends as needed.
Knowledge and understanding of K-20 education systems.
Knowledge of higher education institutions (UC, CSU, CC, etc.) and the ability to interpret policies and procedures to youth, parents, and school representatives. (Preferred)
Ability to maintain cooperative relationships with school district administrators, school counselors, principals, teachers, and community contacts.
